title: First job in Denmark and a new life
summary: His first Danish job was a youth centre where people danced to his kind of music; tours are extended and he makes dozens of albums and a television life story.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah - well for posterity -- good God - I'm not dead yet. But, the point is that when I went to Denmark, I got a shock of my life -- the first

job I played was in the youth center - and I played with a hell of a band; boy, they were marvelous. I couldn't believe my ears. These guys were really laying it down; I had to go a little to catch up and here I'd look out onto the floor and the people are dancing to our kind of music; they hadn't danced to our music in this country in 25 years - they haven't danced to it - our kind of jazz. And, here they are with a brand new dance of their own. Well, man, from that point on, I guess it was a brand new ball game for me.
A whole new world - a whole new life.

Well, it was just like starting my whole life over again; when they asked me to stay; they said - come back; they extended my first tour; couldn't wait 'til I got back to America to come back again and they got me back again and then I started working all the different countries and the money was great; I was recording. I made thirty-one (31) or thirty-two (32) long playing albums over there in the last five years.
You know, I just--- Christ, I've made albums all over the place and I got damn good money for my work; in Denmark they made my life story on a color T.V.---
Yeah - it was an hour-long program. And, uh, I must have done 15 or 20 television shows; I
did concerts with big symphony orchestra - with 35 strings -- with the top radio and television guys in the band; I did everything that I wanted to do in America but never did.
